primitives.name: Zero-Inflated Gamma Snow Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - Short-term (Section 2): zero-inflated gamma regression.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_t': 'snow depth (meters)', 'p_t': 'probability of zero depth (dimensionless)', 'μ_t': 'mean of gamma distribution (meters)', 'σ^2': 'variance of gamma distribution (square meters)', 'β_6, β_7': 'regression coefficients (dimensionless)'}

primitives.name: Physics-Guided Snowfall-Melting Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Physics-structured expectation: - Snowfall: R_t·β0·logit-1(β1 + β2T_t) — inverse-logit snow/rain partition around 0 °C; β0 = estimated snow-water ratio (not fixed at 10).
primitives.latex: S_t = R_t \cdot \beta_0 \cdot \text{logit}^{-1}(\beta_1 + \beta_2 T_t) \quad M_t = D_{t-1} \cdot \text{logit}^{-1}(\beta_3 + (\beta_4 + \beta_5 R_t) T_t)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_t': 'snowfall contribution (meters)', 'M_t': 'melting/aging contribution (meters)', 'R_t': 'precipitation (meters)', 'T_t': 'temperature (°C)', 'D_{t-1}': "previous day's snow depth (meters)", 'β_0': 'snow-water equivalent ratio (dimensionless)', 'β_1, β_2, β_3, β_4, β_5': 'model parameters (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Logistic temperature dependence for phase transition, linear interaction between rain and temperature in melting.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At T_t ≈ 0°C, logit transitions sharply; melting term becomes dominant when R_t > 0 and T_t > 0.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is a zero-inflated gamma regression designed to handle the threshold nature of snow depth—where D_t = 0 occurs frequently due to melting or lack of snowfall. The model decomposes snow depth into two components: a binary process determining whether snow accumulates (P(D_t = 0)) and a continuous process for positive depths (E[D_t|D_t > 0]). This dual structure mirrors the physics of snowfall and melting, which are modeled via logistic and gamma links respectively. The key innovation lies in embedding physical constraints—such as temperature-dependent snow/rain partitioning and rain-temperature interaction in melting—into the likelihood structure. These equations define a generative model for snow depth conditioned on weather inputs. The failure mode arises when weather forecasts are inaccurate or when the assumption of conditional independence breaks down. The model’s strength is its ability to produce probabilistic forecasts directly usable in GSE’s snow-game simulations, where precise field-level snow depth is critical for edge identification.
